content:
Laredo's race for mayor is headed to a runoff.

District 8 Councilwoman Alyssa Cigarroa led the November 3 election with 40.75% of the vote, while incumbent Mayor Dr. Victor Treviño finished second with 32.79%, according to KGNS. Neither reached the 50% needed to win outright, so the two will meet again in a runoff on Saturday, December 12, 2026.

Eight candidates ran for mayor in the November 3 election.

Early voting for the runoff runs December 1 through December 8, 2026.

Cigarroa told KGNS she plans to reach out to all of the candidates and take in their ideas, emphasizing transparency and listening to everyone rather than focusing on one group. She also said she will not ask any candidate to drop out or join her campaign.

Treviño told KGNS the campaign is not over and that he will be more active and work harder in the runoff. He thanked the residents who voted for him and said he remains grateful for the opportunity to serve.

Whoever wins the runoff will be Laredo's next mayor, and once sworn in will help choose a new city manager, according to KGNS.

Sources: KGNS, reporting on the Laredo mayoral runoff on November 4, 2026.

title: Cigarroa, Treviño head to December 12 runoff for Laredo mayor
